# Top 10 EV-Friendly Hotels in Japan: Best Stays with EV Charging 2026

**Last updated: May 27, 2026**

Japan presents a unique challenge for EV travellers. As the birthplace of CHAdeMO — the world's first DC fast-charging standard — Japan has over 40,000 public charging points nationwide, but the landscape is fragmented across multiple networks (e-Power, Toyota Wallet, ENEOS Charge Plus, Nissan ZESP) with different payment apps and RFID cards. The Japanese government has set an ambitious target of 300,000 public charging points by 2030, and competition is driving rapid improvement in hotel EV infrastructure.

Japanese hotels have responded with enthusiasm. Luxury properties in Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka now routinely offer complimentary EV charging, many with dedicated concierge services. Traditional ryokan are increasingly adding destination chargers. The key challenge in Japan is navigating the **CHAdeMO-centric landscape** — while new cars increasingly ship with CCS2 compatibility, the vast majority of Japanese destination charging is still CHAdeMO, and many hotel chargers operate at 6-22 kW AC rather than DC fast charging.

We've ranked Japan's top 10 EV-friendly hotels based on charger speed and quantity, connector compatibility, cost to guests, location convenience, and overall guest experience. Whether you're driving a Nissan Sakura kei-EV through Kyoto's narrow streets, renting a Toyota bZ4X for a Hokkaido road trip, or on business in Tokyo's Marunouchi district, these hotels will keep you charged up.

## Detailed Rankings

### 1. The Ritz-Carlton, Tokyo ⭐ 9.6/10

**Location:** Tokyo Midtown, Akasaka/Ginza, Tokyo
**Charging:** 50 kW DC (CHAdeMO) + 6 kW Type 1 AC (J1772)
**Cost:** Free for hotel guests
**Parking:** Dedicated EV bay on Level B2 (valet-assisted)

The Ritz-Carlton, Tokyo sits in the top floors of Tokyo Midtown Tower, one of Tokyo's most prestigious addresses in Akasaka, minutes from Ginza, Roppongi, and the Imperial Palace. Its **50 kW DC CHAdeMO charger** makes it the most EV-ready luxury hotel in central Tokyo — fast enough for a meaningful top-up while you enjoy the 45th-floor lobby views.

**What makes it #1:**
- **50 kW DC CHAdeMO** — 20-80% in about 60-75 minutes for most EVs (Nissan Sakura, Toyota bZ4X). Leaves you with plenty of range for Tokyo exploration
- **Complimentary for hotel guests** — no additional fee, no surge pricing
- **Tokyo Midtown location** — walk to national art museums, Roppongi nightlife, and the Akasaka Palace grounds
- **Dedicated EV bay** — no competing with non-EV cars for the spot
- **Club Level EV support** — Ritz-Carlton Club concierge can monitor your charging progress and notify you when complete
- **V2H potential** — the CHAdeMO connection supports vehicle-to-home in emergencies (unique for a Tokyo hotel)

**The downside:** 50 kW is moderate by international standards (Korea's Signiel Seoul offers 350 kW). For guests without Japanese EVs, you may need a CHAdeMO adapter (Tesla NACS-to-CHAdeMO adapters available at most rental counters). Only one DC charger — book ahead.

**Best for:** Luxury travellers who want the most EV-ready hotel in central Tokyo with five-star service.

### 2. The Westin Tokyo ⭐ 9.4/10

**Location:** Ebisu, Tokyo (Yebisu Garden Place)
**Charging:** 50 kW DC (CHAdeMO) + 6 kW Type 1 AC (J1772)
**Cost:** Free for hotel guests
**Parking:** 2 EV bays with CHAdeMO + AC combo

The Westin Tokyo delivers an excellent EV experience in the elegant Ebisu district. Located within the Yebisu Garden Place complex — one of Tokyo's most beautiful urban developments — this hotel offers not one but two EV charging bays, making it the most likely luxury Tokyo hotel with **charging availability on arrival**.

**What sets it apart:**
- **2 EV bays** — rare for central Tokyo. Your chance of finding an open charger is significantly higher than any other hotel on this list
- **50 kW DC CHAdeMO + Type 1 AC** — flexibility for any Japanese-market EV or import with CHAdeMO adapter
- **Yebisu Garden Place location** — walk to Ebisu's famous dining scene, the Tokyo Photographic Art Museum, and Ebisu Station (JR Yamanote Line)
- **Westin WORKOUT fitness & pool** — EV charge while you swim — the bay is adjacent to the fitness centre
- **Heavenly Bed for road trip recovery** — Westin's famous bedding is perfect after a long drive into Tokyo
- **Complimentary overnight charging** — unlike some hotels that limit to 2-3 hours, Westin allows overnight charging at no extra cost

**The downside:** Ebisu is 2.5 km from the Shibuya crossing and 4 km from Shinjuku — not walking distance to the busiest areas. The 50 kW DC charger is shared, though the 2-bay setup reduces conflict.

**Best for:** Families and business travellers who want guaranteed EV charging availability in Tokyo.

### 3. Hilton Tokyo ⭐ 9.2/10

**Location:** Nishi-Shinjuku, Tokyo (Shinjuku Station area)
**Charging:** 50 kW DC (CHAdeMO)
**Cost:** Free for hotel guests
**Parking:** 1 dedicated DC EV bay (valet-assisted)

Hilton Tokyo sits in the heart of Shinjuku — Tokyo's busiest business and entertainment district — and offers one of the most conveniently located EV chargers in the city. Steps from Shinjuku Station, Kabukicho, and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck, this is the EV-friendly hotel with the best **central Tokyo walkability**.

**Why it ranks here:**
- **50 kW DC CHAdeMO** in Nishi-Shinjuku — the most strategically located hotel DC charger in Tokyo for exploring west Tokyo
- **Shinjuku location** — walk to Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, Tokyo's best department stores (Isetan, Takashimaya), and the Omoide Yokocho (Piss Alley) dining area
- **Family-friendly** — one of the few Tokyo luxury hotels with dedicated children's amenities and connecting rooms, ideal for EV road trip families
- **830 rooms** — high booking probability, and the valet will manage your charging without you needing to move the car
- **Complimentary** — free for all hotel guests regardless of room category

**The downside:** Only 1 DC charger. Weekend demand means the bay is often occupied. The charger is CHAdeMO-only (no AC backup). If your rental EV doesn't support CHAdeMO or you lack an adapter, you're out of luck.

**Best for:** Shinjuku-centric travellers and families on Japan EV road trips.

### 4. Park Hyatt Tokyo ⭐ 9.0/10

**Location:** Shinjuku (west), Tokyo (Tokyo Opera City Tower)
**Charging:** 50 kW DC (CHAdeMO) + 6 kW AC (Type 1)
**Cost:** Free for hotel guests
**Parking:** 1 DC bay + AC bay, underground parking connected to Tokyo Opera City complex

The Park Hyatt Tokyo — made famous by *Lost in Translation* — remains one of Tokyo's most iconic luxury hotels, and its EV charging setup is among the best in Shinjuku. Perched on the top floors of Tokyo Opera City Tower, the hotel offers 50 kW DC charging with panoramic mountain views from the car park.

**What makes it special:**
- **50 kW DC + AC** — dual-connector flexibility
- **New York Bar & Peak Lounge** — arguably Tokyo's best hotel bar, and the car park entrance is hidden away from the main Shinjuku traffic chaos
- **Tokyo Opera City complex** — concert hall, art museum, and restaurants all connected underground — charge while you culture
- **Western Shinjuku location** — quieter than the east side but a 10-minute walk to Shinjuku Station
- **Generous room sizes** — the largest standard rooms in Tokyo (55 m²+), essential for EV road trip luggage

**The downside:** The charger is in the Tokyo Opera City shared car park, not the hotel's exclusive area. It's shared with office workers during business hours (free after 6 PM typically). Only 1 DC charger.

**Best for:** Luxury seekers and film buffs who want Tokyo's most iconic hotel experience with EV capability.

**Highlights:**
- **2 EV bays** (DC + AC) — better availability than most central Tokyo hotels
- **Tokyo Tower views** — the hotel wraps around the iconic tower, and the sky lobby on the 25th floor is breathtaking
- **Shiba Park setting** — the most park-adjacent hotel in central Tokyo, with Shiba Park's walking paths and Zojoji Temple right outside
- **Large parking area** — easy manoeuvring for larger EVs (no tight underground ramps)
- **Free charging** — no time limit, no hourly fees

**The downside:** The hotel itself is slightly dated compared to newer Tokyo luxury entrants like the Bulgari Hotel Tokyo or Janu Tokyo. The 50 kW DC charger is shared with the attached annex building.

**Best for:** Value-conscious travellers who want guaranteed EV charging near Tokyo's top attractions.

Kyoto — Japan's cultural heart — presents unique challenges for EV travellers. The city's narrow streets, limited parking, and UNESCO World Heritage site restrictions make EV driving both rewarding and tricky. The Ritz-Carlton, Kyoto, on the banks of the Kamogawa River, provides the city's best EV charging experience.

**What sets it apart:**
- **50 kW DC CHAdeMO** — the fastest hotel charger within walking distance of Kyoto's central attractions
- **Kamogawa River location** — walk to the Imperial Palace, Nijo Castle, and Pontocho dining alley
- **Valet handles everything** — no wrestling with CHAdeMO cables in narrow Kyoto parking spaces
- **Complimentary** — free charging included in your stay
- **Pier 7 Restaurant** — one of Kyoto's finest hotel restaurants, with Kamogawa river views

**The downside:** Kyoto itself has limited DC fast charging outside of Nissan dealers and a few public stations. You'll rely heavily on hotel charging. The valet-managed single EV bay means advance reservation is essential.

**Best for:** Luxury travellers exploring Kyoto's cultural treasures by EV.

## Japan EV Hotel Charging: What You Need to Know

### 1. Japan Runs on CHAdeMO — Bring an Adapter

Unlike most of the world, where CCS2 has become the universal DC standard, Japan remains heavily CHAdeMO-centric. Almost all hotel DC chargers are CHAdeMO. If your EV uses CCS2 (common on European and Chinese imports) or NACS (Tesla), you **need a CHAdeMO adapter**. Most car rental companies in Japan (Times Car Rental, Nippon Rent-A-Car) provide them on request, but confirm when booking.

👉 [Buy a CHAdeMO Adapter for Japan Travel on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/?tag=familytravel0d-20)

### 2. Most Hotel Charging is Free (With Caveats)

As in South Korea, most Japanese hotels offer **complimentary EV charging** as a competitive amenity. However:
- Some hotels limit DC charging to 2-3 hours (InterContinental Osaka)
- Some restrict EV bays to suite-level guests
- Ryokan and traditional inns may charge a separate fee (typically ¥500-2,000 / $3-13)
- Always confirm charging policy at booking

### 3. AC Destination Charging is the Norm Overnight

Many Japanese hotels offer 6 kW AC Type 1 (J1772) charging rather than DC fast charging. While slower, **AC overnight charging is reliable and sufficient** for most EV travellers. An overnight AC charge (8 hours × 6 kW = 48 kWh) adds 150-200 km of range — more than enough for a day of city driving.

### 4. Type 1 (J1772) is the AC Standard

Japan uses the **Type 1 / J1772 connector** for AC charging — not the Type 2 (Mennekes) common in Europe. Type 1 is a 5-pin single-phase connector, max 7.4 kW (240V × 32A). Most hotel AC chargers in Japan deliver 6 kW.

### 5. Self-Park vs Valet Charging in Japanese Hotels

| Charging Style | Hotels | Pros | Cons |
|---------------|--------|------|------|
| **Self-park EV bays** | Prince Park Tower, Westin Tokyo, JR Tower Sapporo | Control over connection, pack/unpack freely | Must handle cables yourself |
| **Valet charging** | Ritz-Carlton Tokyo/Kyoto/Fukuoka, Hilton Tokyo, Park Hyatt Tokyo | No cable handling, valet monitors progress | Limited to 1-2 EVs at a time, restricted parking |

### 6. Japan's Expressway Charging (for Hotel-to-Hotel Road Trips)

Japan's expressway rest areas (SA/PA — Service Areas / Parking Areas) are well-equipped with CHAdeMO fast chargers. The **Japan Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Map** (available on the e-Mobility Power app) is essential for route planning.

| Expressway | Route | Key Cities | Charger Density |
|-----------|-------|-----------|----------------|
| Tomei Expressway | Tokyo → Nagoya → Osaka | Yokohama, Shizuoka, Nagoya | Every SA/PA: 2-4 CHAdeMO DC chargers |
| Meishin Expressway | Nagoya → Kyoto → Osaka | Kyoto, Otsu | Every SA/PA: 2-4 CHAdeMO DC chargers |
| Tohoku Expressway | Tokyo → Sendai → Aomori | Utsunomiya, Sendai | Every SA/PA: 2 CHAdeMO DC chargers |
| Hokkaido Expressway | Sapporo → Asahikawa → Wakkanai | Furano, Asahikawa | Sparse — plan ahead, some gaps of 100+ km |
| Kyushu Expressway | Fukuoka → Kumamoto → Kagoshima | Kurume, Kumamoto | Every SA: 2 CHAdeMO DC chargers |

### 7. Winter Charging in Japan

Japanese winters vary dramatically by region. Hokkaido and Tohoku experience heavy snow and sub-zero temperatures (-5°C to -15°C), reducing EV range by 25-35%. Honshu's Pacific coast (Tokyo, Nagoya, Osaka) is milder but still cold (0°C to 7°C). Hotels with **indoor/underground parking** are strongly recommended for winter EV travel — the Ritz-Carlton Tokyo, Hilton Tokyo, and JR Tower Sapporo all offer heated underground parking.

### 8. Kei-Cars and Japan's Unique EV Market

Japan's kei-car segment — tiny, tax-advantaged vehicles — includes the **Nissan Sakura** and **Mitsubishi eK X EV**, Japan's best-selling EVs. These have small batteries (20-30 kWh) and limited road trip range but are perfect for city driving and charge completely overnight on any AC hotel charger. If you're renting a Sakura for Tokyo or Kyoto exploration, any hotel with AC charging will give you a full battery each morning.
